_comment: ARCHITECTURE §7.3 / ADR-004's drift ladder, as amended by ADR-004 Amendment A1: (state, drift, reference, route_state) -> (action, state, error). Boundary rows cover TEST_PLAN §2's 24/25/119/120/121/1999/2000/2001 list in both signs; the sequences are where hysteresis, the 3-seeks-in-60s budget and route suspension become visible at all. Generated by tools/generate_drift_vectors.py — an independent third transcription of the ladder. Edit the generator, never this file.
_invariants: No action other than RESTORE_RATE or NUDGE ever changes the playback rate, and RESTORE_RATE always means exactly 1.0 — 0.998 and 1.002 appear only inside NUDGE.
While route_transitioning the action is always NONE and hard_seek_at_session_us never grows — a route change must not consume the seek budget it did not cause.
A nudge engages at |drift| >= 25 and releases only at |drift| < 15; there is no input that both engages and releases, which is what makes oscillation impossible.
Once failed is true every subsequent action is NONE, whatever the drift.
Every DECLARE_SYNC_FAILURE row leaves nudging false and nudge_rate exactly 1.0.

HARD_SEEK's position_ms is the authoritative timeline's expected position plus the reference's drift against that same timeline plus restart_compensation_ms, floored at 0 (ADR-004 Amendment A1). With a zero reference and nothing learned it is exactly the expected position, which is every pre-amendment row.
Without a usable reference the action is NONE or RESTORE_RATE, never a seek, a nudge or a failure, and error_ms is null: a leader, which has no reference, never corrects.

Any step with route_transitioning, or whose route_change_count differs from the state's route_change_count before it, leaves restart_compensation_ms 0 and pending_seek null — whether playing, paused or failed (PR #32 review).
A reference with at_session_us > now_session_us is never usable: error_ms is null.
A reference whose anchor_session_us or anchor_position_ms differs from the input's is never usable: error_ms is null (PR #32 review round 2).
